newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba - mark broadly reflects economic fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Buba - mark broadly reflects economic fundamentals.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday the mark has fallen to a level that roughly reflects underlying economic fundamentals.

The German central bank, in its monthly report for June, said the mark was now weaker against 18 major currencies than it was in early 1995 -- a period that marked the start of a steady appreciation of the German currency.
"In comparably quiet currency markets, mark levels have prevailed that should to a great extent reflect economic fundamentals," the Bundesbank said in the monthly report.
The dollar was trading at 1.7350 marks in late European dealings on Tuesday.
The appreciation of the dollar since the start of the year has not had a detrimental affect on the German capital markets, the Bundesbank added.
"Capital market participants obviously see this as normalisation (of the mark) but no indication of lasting weakening in the mark," the report said.
The report also said current low interest rates in Germany were due to "favourable inflation prospects and the rather moderate growth dynamic in the economy".
"The normalisatiion of currency relationships has, in view of the broad front of low interest rates, brightend the monetary environment for a strengthening of economic growth," the Bundesbank said.
